messages.content: The client just moved the workshop from Center City to their King of Prussia office. We leave in two days. Can you compare keeping the Sonesta with switching to something near the new site? Include the commute and what each choice does to airport costs.
Yes. What is the new office address, and has the Sonesta reservation now been completed? I also need its current cancellation deadline from the confirmation.
It’s 1150 First Avenue, King of Prussia. The Sonesta is booked at the $742.11 total we reviewed. The confirmation says I can cancel without penalty until tomorrow at 4:00 p.m. Eastern.

I found two nearby candidates still under the $245 nightly cap: Hyatt House Philadelphia/King of Prussia at $224 per night, $757.68 total, and Crowne Plaza Philadelphia-King of Prussia at $206 per night, $699.42 total. Both show refundable rates through 6:00 p.m. Eastern tomorrow. The Hyatt House is about 1.2 miles from the office; the Crowne Plaza is about 2.4 miles away. I’m checking total ground transportation next.
Assume rideshare. I don’t want to add a rental car this late.

For the Sonesta, PHL rideshare is approximately $35-$50 each way. The new office commute is roughly 22-27 miles and typically 40-70 minutes each way during workshop hours, with estimated rideshare fares of $55-$85 per trip. Across three workshop days, that puts ground transportation around $400-$610, including the airport legs.

From either suburban hotel, PHL rideshare is approximately $60-$85 each way. Daily hotel-office rideshares should be about $10-$18 each way from Hyatt House or $12-$22 each way from Crowne Plaza. Estimated trip totals are $180-$278 for Hyatt House and $192-$302 for Crowne Plaza.
So the city hotel is cheaper to the airport but much worse overall. What are the combined hotel and transportation estimates?

Sonesta: $742.11 hotel plus about $400-$610 transportation, for $1,142.11-$1,352.11. Hyatt House: $757.68 plus about $180-$278, for $937.68-$1,035.68. Crowne Plaza: $699.42 plus about $192-$302, for $891.42-$1,001.42.

The Crowne Plaza has the lowest projected total. Hyatt House costs about $46-$58 more overall but is closer to the office, trimming roughly 5-10 minutes from each local ride. Both avoid the unpredictable Center City-to-King of Prussia rush-hour commute.
Does either one have a hotel shuttle to that office?

The Hyatt House listing advertises a local shuttle within a limited radius, but the operating hours and whether 1150 First Avenue is included require confirmation with the hotel. The Crowne Plaza listing does not promise a general local shuttle. I have treated all local trips as paid rideshares, so the comparison does not depend on shuttle availability.
Choose the Hyatt House. The shorter daily trip is worth the small difference. Make sure I don’t end up holding both rooms.

I can sequence it as follows: first secure the refundable Hyatt House room at $757.68 total, then cancel the Sonesta and retain both confirmation records. Before I submit either action, confirm that I should proceed with the Hyatt House booking and Sonesta cancellation now.

The Hyatt House Philadelphia/King of Prussia reservation is confirmed for Monday, July 27 through Thursday, July 30, 2026, for three nights at $757.68 including currently disclosed taxes and mandatory fees. Its confirmation shows penalty-free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. Eastern on Saturday, July 25.

The Sonesta Philadelphia Rittenhouse Square reservation has been canceled before its deadline. The cancellation record shows no penalty and release of the one-night deposit; the posting time for the credit depends on the card issuer. There is no longer an active room at the Sonesta.

Using rideshares, projected hotel and ground transportation is $937.68-$1,035.68. That is approximately $106-$414 less than keeping the city hotel, while removing the long rush-hour commute. The American flights remain unchanged. Confirm the Hyatt House local shuttle hours and coverage directly with the property; the cost estimate already assumes paid rideshares for every local trip.
